metadata_atomic_policy.reason: The pinned ml-100k load_col consumes only .inter. The official README does not fully resolve raw metadata delimiter/encoding behavior needed for a byte-precise metadata conversion, and no such metadata is needed by the selected BPR consumer surface.
metadata_atomic_policy.future_change_rule: Any future .item or .user conversion requires a separately frozen transform, raw-byte parser receipt, and explicit schema mapping; it cannot be inferred from repository blobs.

raw_to_atomic_reconciliation_checks.requirement: Archive byte count equals 4,924,029; recomputed MD5 equals the current official sidecar; locally computed SHA-256 and byte count are recorded.
Exactly the 23 allowlisted regular files exist under raw/ml-100k; every file has byte count and SHA-256.
Parsed u.info equals 943 users, 1,682 items, and 100,000 ratings.
Every non-empty u.data line has exactly four TAB-separated fields satisfying the declared decimal constraints.
Atomic data-row count is 100,000 and raw row n maps only to atomic row n+1 after the single header.
For every ordinal, all four atomic lexical values equal the corresponding raw lexical values exactly.
Compute SHA-256 for raw and atomic over the same canonical stream ordinal NUL user NUL item NUL rating NUL timestamp LF; require equality.
Observed raw and atomic user token sets are exactly decimal 1..943; item token sets are exactly decimal 1..1682; no unknown, missing, or duplicate domain token.
Record duplicate user-item pair count and fail if nonzero; never silently deduplicate.
First-occurrence expected maps contain [PAD]=0 plus exactly 943 user and 1,682 item tokens, and every token round-trips.
The normative atomic directory contains exactly ml-100k.inter; receipts and ID maps live outside the consumer dataset directory.

future_diagnostic_sequence: Only after a separate source-blob materialization authorization, bind each repository blob by revision, Git object ID, raw byte count, and local SHA-256.
Compare repository .inter header, row count, ordered lexical fields, canonical projection digest, and full bytes against the normative GroupLens-derived .inter.
